name: Amoxicillin/clavulanic acid
executiveSummary: Beta-lactam + inhibitor. Adult PO 875/125 mg every 12 h or 500/125 every 8 h; IV 1.2 g every 8 h. Pediatrics by amoxicillin component: 20–40 mg/kg/day (high-risk otitis 80–90 mg/kg/day).
indications:
## Indications

- Respiratory infections, otitis media, sinusitis, skin/soft tissue, and UTI due to susceptible beta-lactamase–producing organisms.
- Bites and selected polymicrobial infections per antibiogram.

## Precautions

- Diarrhea / *C. difficile*; hepatotoxicity (more with prolonged courses).
- Adjust in renal failure. Penicillin allergy: contraindicated.
- Always calculate by the **amoxicillin component**; verify presentation ratio (7:1 duo vs 4:1).

> Duo presentations (875/125 or 80/11.4 mg/mL suspension) are given every 12 h.

adulto.presentation: Tablets 500/125 and 875/125 mg; suspension; IV 1.2 g (1000/200) or 2.2 g by brand.
adulto.dose: PO: **875/125 mg every 12 h** or **500/125 mg every 8 h**. More severe: keep 875/125 q12h or escalate to IV. IV: **1.2 g every 8 h** (severe: up to **1.2 g every 6 h** or **2.2 g every 8 h** per label/ID).
adulto.administration: PO at the start of meals (better GI tolerance). IV: reconstitute and dilute per label; usual intermittent infusion 30–40 min.
adulto.notes: Does not cover ESBL or MRSA. Complete the course even if symptoms improve.

pediatrico.presentation: Suspension 4:1 (e.g. 50/12.5 mg/mL) or duo 7:1 (e.g. 80/11.4 mg/mL); tablets 500/125 and 875/125.
pediatrico.dose: By **amoxicillin**: mild–moderate **20–40 mg/kg/day** divided every 8 h (4:1) or every 12 h (7:1 duo). High-risk/persistent otitis: **80–90 mg/kg/day** amoxicillin (duo q12h). Usual max **~90 mg/kg/day** amoxicillin; absolute ceilings often **2–3 g/day** amoxicillin by severity and label.
pediatrico.administration: PO. Shake suspension; refrigerate after reconstitution per label.
pediatrico.notes: Verify mg/mL before measuring. Do not use duo for a 4:1 regimen without recalculating.

neonatal.dose: Not routine; only under NNU/ID with dose and interval by gestational/postnatal age.
neonatal.administration: PO or IV by tolerance and severity.
neonatal.notes: Early-onset neonatal sepsis empiric therapy is usually ampicillin + gentamicin, not amox-clav.

stability:
## Stability

- Reconstituted suspension: refrigerate per label (usually 7–10 days).
- Diluted IV: use within the shift / per manufacturer stability.
adverseEffects:
## Adverse effects

Diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, candidiasis, rash, elevated transaminases. Rare: cholestatic hepatitis, interstitial nephritis, blood dyscrasias, anaphylaxis.
